item.title: Activists battle to preserve Kinshasa’s last Baobab
item.description: Once shaded by trees, Kinshasa has steadily lost its greenery to unchecked development, pollution, and population pressure. However, a lone century-old baobab tree, near the ferry port in Gombe, stands as a living monument to the city’s past. item.title: Senegal exceeds oil and gas expectations
item.description: Senegal’s oil sector delivered a great surprise in 2025, with crude production climbing to 36.1 million barrels, comfortably beating initial forecasts by nearly 6 million barrels. Earlier estimates had already been revised upward, but output still outpaced expectations thanks to resilient reservoirs, well-maintained wells, and efficient operations. item.title: Moroccan cave discovery may rewrite human history
item.description: A newly dated set of hominin fossils from a cave in Casablanca, Morocco, may help close a long-standing gap in the story of human evolution. item.description: Somaliland has reentered the global spotlight after Israel became the first country to formally recognize the breakaway region as an independent state, a move that could reshape Horn of Africa geopolitics. item.description: DR Congo’s AFCON 2025 journey ended in extra-time heartbreak against Algeria, but one supporter left the tournament as an unforgettable symbol.
